tagline: A forest road links a mill town and a reservoir crossing
intro: The Elk River Backcountry Byway winds through evergreen forest in the Clearwater Mountains and crosses Dworshak Reservoir on Dent Bridge. Visit Idaho includes it among the state’s scenic byways and gives the one-way drive two hours. The drive has dips and turns, with farmsteads and patches of timber along Wells Bench. The reservoir crossing is a two-lane suspension bridge, with a main span of 1,050 feet.

When Potlatch Lumber Company reached Elk River in 1906, no roads led into the backcountry; logs traveled down the North Fork of the Clearwater during spring runoff. The later construction of Dworshak Dam required a new crossing to preserve vehicle access to Elk River. The Army Corps of Engineers built Dent Bridge in place of a smaller bridge over the river. Construction began in December 1969, and materials for the new crossing had to come over winding logging roads. The work required hauling more than 20,000 cubic yards of concrete and 4,150 tons of steel into the backcountry.

Start at Bovill and follow Idaho 8 to Elk River, the former sawmill town. Near Elk River, the cedar grove is reached from Forest Road 382. Continue toward Dent Bridge and the reservoir, then climb through forest to Wells Bench before descending to Orofino.

moments.title: Elk River
moments.text: Elk River’s sawmill had a pond built expressly for its logs. The town had begun as a hunting resort before becoming a lumber town in 1909. Potlatch dammed Elk Creek in 1910, creating storage where timber brought by horse skid or sleigh could float, protected from insects and drying. The mill used electric power, and the town grew rapidly after Potlatch opened it. Its Potlatch sawmill was phased out during the 1930s. A three-mile Loop Road follows part of the original railroad grade between Elk River and Bovill, the rail connection that served the sawmill.

moments.title: Giant Western Redcedar
moments.text: The giant western redcedar belongs to an old-growth grove reached by Trail 748. The tree is 177 feet tall and 18 feet in diameter, with an estimated age of 3,000 years. Nearby, Trail 749 makes a three-quarter-mile loop among 500-year-old trees in an 80-acre grove.

moments.title: Dent Bridge
moments.text: Dent Bridge replaced a river crossing that the new reservoir would flood. Completed in 1971, the two-lane suspension bridge measures 1,550 feet overall, with a main span of 1,050 feet. Its name comes from Charles and Katherine Dent, who owned land on the western side in 1895. The settlement of Dent was razed before the reservoir flooded it. Building the new bridge preserved access between the Orofino side of the Clearwater and Elk River. Its site was chosen for terrain that would accommodate both the bridge itself and the roads needed to reach it.
